## Overview

Spatial transcriptomics tissue sections are not truly 2D — they typically
have a physical thickness of 4–10 µm. Cells can partially overlap along
the z-dimension, causing transcript contamination between overlapping cells.
This module quantifies how well each segmentation method resolves 3D cell
overlaps.

## Z distribution of transcripts

Distribution of transcripts across z-planes. Xenium data may show z-drift
(uneven distribution across depth), while Proseg v3 corrects for this
internally.

```{python}
def plot_transcripts_across_z_bins(sdata, method, n_z_bins=10, xy_bin_size=5.0):
    df = sdata["transcripts"].compute()
    df["z_bin"] = pd.cut(df["z"], n_z_bins, labels=False)
    df["x_bin"] = (df["x"] / xy_bin_size).astype(int)
    df["y_bin"] = (df["y"] / xy_bin_size).astype(int)

    x_minb, x_maxb = df["x_bin"].min(), df["x_bin"].max()
    y_minb, y_maxb = df["y_bin"].min(), df["y_bin"].max()
    nx = x_maxb - x_minb + 1
    ny = y_maxb - y_minb + 1

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
        1, n_z_bins,
        figsize=(2.2 * n_z_bins, 4),
        sharex=True, sharey=True,
        constrained_layout=True
    )
    axes = np.atleast_1d(axes)

    for i in range(n_z_bins):
        ax = axes[i]
        plane = df[df["z_bin"] == i]
        counts = (
            plane.groupby(["y_bin", "x_bin"])
            .size()
            .reindex(
                pd.MultiIndex.from_product(
                    [range(y_minb, y_maxb + 1), range(x_minb, x_maxb + 1)],
                    names=["y_bin", "x_bin"]
                ),
                fill_value=0,
            )
            .values.reshape(ny, nx)
        )
        im = ax.imshow(counts, origin="lower", aspect="equal")
        ax.set_title(f"Z {i+1}")
        ax.set_xlabel("x")
        if i == 0:
            ax.set_ylabel("y")

    cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes.ravel().tolist(), location="right", shrink=0.9)
    cbar.set_label(f"# transcripts per {xy_bin_size}x{xy_bin_size} bin")
    fig.suptitle(f"{method}: transcripts per z-plane", fontsize=14)
    plt.show()

for method, st in st_dict.items():
    plot_transcripts_across_z_bins(st.sdata, method, n_z_bins=10)
```

## Top-bottom z consistency

For each cell, transcripts are split into a bottom (z ≤ q30) and top
(z ≥ q70) fraction. The cosine similarity between the two expression
profiles measures whether the cell contains a consistent transcriptome
across depth. Low similarity suggests 3D overlap or transcript contamination.

Note: z-drift correction is disabled for Proseg v3 as it already corrects
for z-drift internally.

```{python}
for method, st in st_dict.items():
    correct_z = False if "proseg" in method else True
    st.vl.similarity_top_bottom(correct_z_drift=correct_z)
    print(f"{method}: top-bottom z similarity computed")
```

```{python}
dfs = []
for method, st in st_dict.items():
    obs = st.sdata.tables["table"].obs.copy()
    obs["method"] = method
    dfs.append(obs[["method", "cosine_sim_top_bottom_z"]].dropna())

df_all = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
sns.kdeplot(
    data=df_all,
    x="cosine_sim_top_bottom_z",
    hue="method",
    palette="Set2",
    common_norm=False,
    fill=False,
    ax=ax
)
ax.set_title("Top-bottom z consistency (cosine similarity)")
ax.set_xlabel("Cosine similarity")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
# Relationship between transcript count and top-bottom similarity
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(st_dict), figsize=(6 * len(st_dict), 4))
if len(st_dict) == 1:

for ax, (method, st) in zip(axes, st_dict.items()):
    df = st.sdata.tables["table"].obs[
        ["cosine_sim_top_bottom_z", "transcript_count"]
    ].dropna()
    sns.regplot(
        data=df,
        x="transcript_count",
        y="cosine_sim_top_bottom_z",
        scatter_kws={"alpha": 0.3, "s": 5},
        line_kws={"color": "red"},
        lowess=True,
        ci=None,
        ax=ax
    )
    ax.set_title(f"{method}")
    ax.set_xlabel("Transcript count")
    ax.set_ylabel("cosine_sim_top_bottom_z")

fig.suptitle("Top-bottom z similarity vs transcript count", y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Vertical Signal Integrity (VSI)

VSI (ovrlpy) computes a pixel-level map of vertical signal integrity —
regions where the transcriptome is consistent across depth (high VSI)
versus regions prone to 3D mixing (low VSI). We compute mean VSI per cell
by averaging VSI values at each transcript's (x,y) position.

```{python}
# Compute VSI map once on Xenium data
def run_ovrlpy(sdata, n_comp, points_gene_key="feature_name", n_workers=4):
    coordinate_df = sdata["transcripts"].compute()
    coordinate_df = coordinate_df.rename(columns={points_gene_key: "gene"})
    coordinate_df = coordinate_df[["gene", "x", "y", "z"]]
    coordinate_df["z"] = coordinate_df["z"] - coordinate_df["z"].min()
    ovrlpy_sdata = ovrlpy.Ovrlp(
        coordinate_df, n_components=n_comp, n_workers=n_workers, random_state=42
    )
    ovrlpy_sdata.analyse()
    return ovrlpy_sdata.integrity_map

n_genes = st_dict["xenium"].sdata.tables["table"].n_vars
print(f"Computing VSI map on Xenium data ({n_genes} genes)...")
vsi_map = run_ovrlpy(st_dict["xenium"].sdata, n_comp=min(10, n_genes))
print("VSI map computed")
```

```{python}
for method, st in st_dict.items():
    st.vl.vertical_signal_integrity_per_cell(vsi_map)
    print(f"{method}: VSI per cell computed")
```

```{python}
dfs = []
for method, st in st_dict.items():
    obs = st.sdata.tables["table"].obs.copy()
    obs["method"] = method
    dfs.append(obs[["method", "vertical_signal_integrity"]].dropna())

df_all = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
sns.kdeplot(
    data=df_all,
    x="vertical_signal_integrity",
    hue="method",
    palette="Set2",
    common_norm=False,

ax.set_title("Vertical Signal Integrity per cell")
ax.set_xlabel("VSI")

```

```{python}
# VSI vs top-bottom z similarity
n = len(st_dict)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, n, figsize=(5 * n, 4), sharey=True)
axes = np.atleast_1d(axes)

for ax, (method, st) in zip(axes, st_dict.items()):
    df = st.sdata.tables["table"].obs[
        ["vertical_signal_integrity", "cosine_sim_top_bottom_z", "transcript_count"]
    ].dropna()
    df = df[df["transcript_count"] > df["transcript_count"].quantile(0.1)]

    r = np.corrcoef(df["vertical_signal_integrity"], df["cosine_sim_top_bottom_z"])[0, 1]
    r2 = r ** 2

    sns.regplot(
        data=df,
        x="vertical_signal_integrity",
        y="cosine_sim_top_bottom_z",
        scatter_kws={"alpha": 0.3, "s": 5},
        line_kws={"color": "red"},
        ci=95,
        ax=ax
    )
    ax.set_title(f"{method} (R² = {r2:.3f})")
    ax.set_xlabel("Vertical Signal Integrity")
    ax.set_ylabel("cosine_sim_top_bottom_z")

fig.suptitle("VSI vs top-bottom z consistency", y=1.02)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Heterotypic overlap (Proseg only)

This metric quantifies where Proseg detects overlaps between cells of
different types across z-layers. It requires per-z-layer cell polygons
and is therefore only available for Proseg v3.

```{python}
proseg_dict = {k: v for k, v in st_dict.items() if "proseg" in k}

if proseg_dict and has_reference:
    for method, st in proseg_dict.items():
        st.vl.fraction_heterotypic_overlap(unknown_policy="exclude")
        print(f"{method}: heterotypic overlap computed")
elif proseg_dict and not has_reference:
    print("Heterotypic overlap requires a scRNA-seq reference (has_reference: true). Skipping.")
else:
    print("No Proseg method found — skipping heterotypic overlap.")
```

```{python}
if proseg_dict and has_reference:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))

    dfs_area = []
    dfs_frac = []
    for method, st in proseg_dict.items():
        obs = st.sdata.tables["table"].obs.copy()
        obs["method"] = method
        dfs_area.append(obs[["method", "heterotypic_overlap_area"]].dropna())
        dfs_frac.append(obs[["method", "heterotypic_overlap_fraction"]].dropna())

    df_area = pd.concat(dfs_area, ignore_index=True)
    df_frac = pd.concat(dfs_frac, ignore_index=True)

    sns.kdeplot(
        data=df_area, x="heterotypic_overlap_area",
        hue="method", palette="Set2", common_norm=False, fill=False, ax=axes[0]
    )
    axes[0].set_title("Heterotypic overlap area")

    sns.kdeplot(
        data=df_frac, x="heterotypic_overlap_fraction",
        hue="method", palette="Set2", common_norm=False, fill=False, ax=axes[1]
    )
    axes[1].set_title("Heterotypic overlap fraction")

    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
else:
    print("Section skipped.")
```

## Summary table

```{python}
from utils.helpers import save_metrics
save_metrics(st_dict)

rows = []
for method, st in st_dict.items():
    obs = st.sdata.tables["table"].obs
    row = {"Method": method}

    if "cosine_sim_top_bottom_z" in obs:
        row["Median top-bottom z similarity (↑)"] = round(
            obs["cosine_sim_top_bottom_z"].median(), 3
        )
    if "vertical_signal_integrity" in obs:
        row["Median VSI (↑)"] = round(
            obs["vertical_signal_integrity"].median(), 3
        )
    if "heterotypic_overlap_fraction" in obs:
        row["Median heterotypic overlap fraction (↓)"] = round(
            obs["heterotypic_overlap_fraction"].median(), 3
        )

    rows.append(row)

pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("Method")
```
